tracks.title: Ignition: The Forger's Call
tracks.discName: Act I: The Alma Mater Opening (with the CPI Marching Forgers)
tracks.suiteName: Act I: The Alma Mater Opening
tracks.loreNote: The very first time in history that **"Ignition: The Forger's Call"** was ever played and recorded for a live concert release (previously, the only way to hear *Ignition* was to attend a CPI Home Football Game in person inside **The Crucible**). With no opening act—just CPI Alumni (*Class of 1989*) coming home to play for their alma mater—Ryan O'Connell rolls out to the edge of the stage in his manual chair, recalls the 1986 student contest cassette protected by 16-year-old Holly O'Connell's `$1.00` Perpetual Mutual Cross-License, and cues the stadium blackout. As Tyler strikes his steel brake drum and 65,000 Ironheads execute **The Stomp** on the galvanized bleachers of **The Anvil** until the Copernicus Hall seismographs spike, the four-piece rock band and the 300-piece **CPI Marching Forgers** erupt into a deafening call-and-response of **"IGNITION!"**

tracks.title: CPI Tech Triumph: The Marching Forgers
tracks.discName: Act I: The Alma Mater Opening (with the CPI Marching Forgers)
tracks.suiteName: Act I: The Alma Mater Opening
tracks.loreNote: Directly out of the final anvil strike of *"Ignition"*, the Drum Major's whistle pierces the night air (`Tweet-Tweet-Tweet-Tweet!`) and **"The Engine Room"**—the high-tension Kevlar marching snare battery of the 300-piece **CPI Marching Forgers**—launches into the official Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute Fight Song. Forming the **CPI Hammer and Anvil** across the turf while 65,000 students and alumni clap in time and roar *"GO! FORGERS! FIGHT! FORGERS! WIN! CPI!"*, the Marching Forgers turn the opening minutes of the concert into the ultimate Saturday night inside The Crucible.

tracks.title: The Stardust Engine
tracks.discName: Act I: The Alma Mater Opening (with the CPI Marching Forgers)
tracks.suiteName: Act I: The Alma Mater Opening
tracks.loreNote: While standard Stardust Engine concerts open directly with **"The Stardust Engine"**, here at their alma mater it serves as the culminating third movement of the opening sequence—performed with all 300 members of the **CPI Marching Forgers** still on the stage! Harmonizing 300 collegiate brass instruments and sousaphones with Cassidy's iconic 1986 **"Stardust"** analog synthesizer leitmotif and locking the Kevlar snare battery to Ryan's **"Engine"** guitar and Tyler's gated drums, the performance brings the stadium to a fever pitch before the Marching Forgers march off through the field tunnel—convincing everyone in the building that their guest appearance for the night is over.

tracks.title: Main Engine Start
tracks.discName: Act II: The Reignition & Freedom Era Rock Block
tracks.loreNote: As the Marching Forgers clear the field, the core four-piece band—Cassidy on her wraparound synthesizers, Ryan in his manual chair at stage left on lead guitar, and identical twins Evan (bass) and Tyler (drums) on the back risers—slams straight into the 142 BPM countdown thriller from 2015's *Reignition*. Sixty-five thousand fans count down from ten to liftoff in unison.

tracks.title: Hard Reset
tracks.discName: Act II: The Reignition & Freedom Era Rock Block
tracks.loreNote: Rewinding to the 1997 title track that launched their independent stadium era after buying out their masters in 1996, Ryan and Cassidy trade blistering verses over Evan and Tyler's pounding arena rhythm section.

tracks.title: Not Your Doll
tracks.discName: Act II: The Reignition & Freedom Era Rock Block
tracks.loreNote: Cassidy steps to the front microphone for her fierce 1989 *Neon Hearts* rebellion against the corporate record executives who tried to package her as a fragile pop idol—reclaimed here with full-throttle 1980s hard-rock guitars and analog synth brass.

tracks.title: Static
tracks.discName: Act II: The Reignition & Freedom Era Rock Block
tracks.loreNote: From 1995's independent cassette release *The Warehouse Tapes*. Ryan dedicates the song to the Class of '89 and the original CPI dormitory tape-traders who kept the band alive during the 1992–1995 Wilderness Years.

tracks.title: Midnight Drivers
tracks.discName: Act II: The Reignition & Freedom Era Rock Block
tracks.loreNote: As twilight deepens into blue hour over the Appalachian ridges behind the stadium press box, the band launches into the nocturnal title anthem of 2001's *Midnight Drivers*, honoring Evan and Tyler's decades behind the wheel on I-81.

tracks.title: Fifty-Two to Nothing: The Norfolk Reckoning
tracks.discName: Act II: The Reignition & Freedom Era Rock Block
tracks.loreNote: One of the loudest moments of the entire two-hour show. Pointing up at the North End Zone scoreboard of The Crucible—where sophomore **Jordan Shawn Kelly** (sitting in Accessible Field Section 104, Row A) had suffered his catastrophic `38–0` Homecoming meltdown against Virginia Dominion University (VDU) in September 2014—Ryan and Cassidy unleash the stadium stomper from 2015's *Reignition* celebrating CPI's retaliatory **52–0 shutout victory** in Norfolk, permanently overwriting the `38–0` ghost with 65,000 Forgers roaring *"FIFTY-TWO TO NOTHING! PUT IT ON THE BOARD!"*

tracks.title: The Contract
tracks.discName: Act III: The Vault & Twin Moons Cosmic Block
tracks.loreNote: Because they are playing at home for their alma mater, the band digs deep into 2007's archival vault compilation *Lost Sounds*—performing **"The Contract"** live as a tribute to younger sister and CEO **Holly O'Connell** watching from the side of the stage.

tracks.title: Steel and Synthetics
tracks.discName: Act III: The Vault & Twin Moons Cosmic Block
tracks.loreNote: A second live rarity pulled from 2007's *Lost Sounds* vault compilation, spotlighting the high-voltage interplay between Cassidy's analog synthesizer rig and Ryan's overdriven electric guitar.

tracks.title: Moon 1: Tidal Lock
tracks.discName: Act III: The Vault & Twin Moons Cosmic Block
tracks.loreNote: The stadium floodlights dim to a deep cosmic indigo as Cassidy bathes all 65,000 fans in the zero-gravity analog pads of **The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™** (from 1997's *Hard Reset* and 2003's *Sanctuary [Zero-G]*), turning the entire bowl of The Crucible into a glowing planetarium under the Blacksburg stars.

tracks.title: Mayday: The Intercept
tracks.discName: Act III: The Vault & Twin Moons Cosmic Block
tracks.loreNote: Transitioning directly from *Moon 1* into the heavy, high-friction arena rock of 2003's *Moon 2: Mile Marker 98*, Ryan and Cassidy sing the story of how their family intercepted the darkness after the 1990 Des Moines bus crash and brought everyone home alive.

tracks.title: Our Own Frequency
tracks.discName: Act IV: Our Own Frequency (Intimate Acoustic Block)
tracks.loreNote: **Act IV: *Our Own Frequency* — The Intimate Brother & Sister Acoustic Block (Part 1 of 3).** Recorded in complete secrecy in the living room of the Blacksburg house during the middle of the band's decade-long Burnout Hiatus, 2008's *Our Own Frequency* was never toured, promoted, or accompanied by press interviews—Ryan and Cassidy simply uploaded it to the Engine Room Records website on a Tuesday morning with a one-sentence note: *"We're still here, and we're okay."* At the midpoint of *Live at the Crucible*, Evan and Tyler leave the stage completely, and the towering stadium light rigs dim to two solitary warm spotlights at center stage: Ryan in his wheelchair with an acoustic guitar, Cassidy at the piano, and two microphones. For the first time in front of a live audience, brother and sister strip away the stadium walls of sound to share their most private living-room conversation with their CPI family.

tracks.title: Brother's Keeper
tracks.discName: Act IV: Our Own Frequency (Intimate Acoustic Block)
tracks.loreNote: **Act IV Centerpiece: *"Brother's Keeper"* — The Intimate Reality of Ryan's ADLs & The Final World Tour / CPI Summer Festival Residency Announcement (Part 2 of 3).** The emotional centerpiece of 2008's *Our Own Frequency* and the most private, vulnerable song Ryan and Cassidy have ever written. *"Brother's Keeper"* is an unflinchingly intimate look at the life-or-death mutual protection between brother and sister and what Cassidy and the family go through every single day taking care of Ryan's **ADLs (Activities of Daily Living)** due to his T10 paralysis—performing his daily toileting requirements and morning anti-atrophy leg stretches, pushing his wheelchair when the road is steep, and sharing a bed pushed against the wall at night with Ryan on the inside and Cassidy sleeping on the outside edge to act as a **human bed-rail** so he doesn't roll off, while Ryan serves as Cassidy's emotional anchor against the overwhelming sensory and psychological toll of the world. Before playing the song in the pin-drop silence of The Crucible, Ryan explains that because of the daily physical toll of those ADLs on the road as they have gotten older, the *Reignition* tour is the **last world tour they will ever do**—and announces that starting next summer, The Stardust Engine will stay home in Blacksburg to headline the annual **CPI Summer Festival** as a permanent Hometown Residency.

tracks.title: Safe Person
tracks.discName: Act IV: Our Own Frequency (Intimate Acoustic Block)
tracks.loreNote: **Act IV: *Our Own Frequency* — The Intimate Brother & Sister Acoustic Block (Part 3 of 3).** Completing the three-song *Our Own Frequency* (2008) living-room trilogy, **"Safe Person"** answers the physical devotion of *"Brother's Keeper"* by revealing the other half of their unbreakable bond: how Ryan acts as Cassidy's safe person and emotional anchor when the flashing cameras, press questions, and autistic sensory overload threaten to overwhelm her. Performed strictly by Ryan on acoustic guitar and Cassidy at the piano with zero electric amps or stadium lights, sixty-five thousand Forgers hold up quiet white phone lights across the dark bowl of The Crucible.

tracks.title: Echoes in the Wire
tracks.discName: Act V: Saturday Night Lights & The Homecoming Sprint
tracks.loreNote: **Act V Opener: Full-Band Electric Return (Permanently Replacing *"If You Walked Away"*).** Following the three-song *Our Own Frequency* brother-and-sister acoustic block, Evan and Tyler walk back onto the stage and strap on their electric bass and drum kit. Because 1989's *"If You Walked Away"* is permanently banned from all post-1990 Stardust Engine concerts to protect Cassidy from autistic sensory and abandonment overload, **"Echoes in the Wire"** (from 1997's *Hard Reset*) holds the emotional power-ballad spotlight—beginning at Cassidy's grand piano before Evan, Tyler, and Ryan's full electric stadium rig roars back to life.

tracks.title: Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible
tracks.discName: Act V: Saturday Night Lights & The Homecoming Sprint
tracks.loreNote: **THE LIVE CONCERT DEBUT.** Although the studio recording of **"Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible"** (from 2004's *Progress Street*) first blasted over the stadium PA between the 3rd and 4th quarters on October 8, 2004, the band vowed they would **ONLY ever perform the song live when playing inside The Crucible** (deliberately omitting it even from 2005's *Live in Norfolk*). As the four massive Ironstone floodlight towers blaze at 100% power to kick off the fourth-quarter sprint of the concert, The Stardust Engine unleashes the live concert debut of *"Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible"* to a 65,000-voice roar of *"GO FORGERS! GO CPI!"*

tracks.title: Progress Street: Where the Fire Began
tracks.discName: Act V: Saturday Night Lights & The Homecoming Sprint
tracks.loreNote: Singing about the house on Progress Street NE just a mile and a half north of the stadium, Ryan and Cassidy lead the entire lower bowl and student section in a jubilant 1980s AOR hometown singalong.

tracks.title: Neon Hearts
tracks.discName: Act V: Saturday Night Lights & The Homecoming Sprint
tracks.loreNote: The band's 1989 hit title track, performed with the soaring 1980s arena-rock guitars and analog synth brass the band always wanted.

tracks.title: My Anchor Holds
tracks.discName: Act V: Saturday Night Lights & The Homecoming Sprint
tracks.loreNote: One of the signature anthems from 1987's *Electric Color*, with 65,000 voices singing every word of the chorus back to the stage.

tracks.title: Reignition: Lights On on Progress Street
tracks.discName: Act V: Saturday Night Lights & The Homecoming Sprint
tracks.loreNote: The triumphant opening title anthem of 2015's *Reignition*, celebrating the family's return from their ten-year Burnout Hiatus and the permanent homecoming ahead in Blacksburg.

tracks.title: Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street
tracks.discName: Act V: Saturday Night Lights & The Homecoming Sprint
tracks.loreNote: **THE FALSE ENDING.** To close what the audience believes is the end of the concert (and the final stop of their last world tour before beginning their annual CPI Summer Festival residency), the band performs the grand stadium power-ballad finale of 2004's *Progress Street*. As the drums and guitars slowly fade to a lone upright piano chord, Cassidy whispers *"Lights out on Progress Street..."*, Ryan says *"Goodnight, Forger Nation,"* and every stage light and Jumbotron screen inside The Crucible cuts to pitch black—convincing 65,000 fans that the concert is over.

tracks.title: Electric Color
tracks.discName: Act VI: The True Ending (with the CPI Marching Forgers)
tracks.loreNote:
The secret 5-minute-26-second **Actual Ending** of the May 21, 2016 homecoming concert inside **The Crucible**—and the very first time in the band's 30-year history that **"Electric Color"** was ever performed as the blistering **1980s Album-Oriented Rock (Stadium Rock)** anthem Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler originally heard in their heads before Apex Records forced them to release it as a glossy 1987 Dance Synth-Pop single.

Right after the false ending of **"Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street"** plunged the stadium into darkness, all 300 members of the **CPI Marching Forgers** marched back out onto the stage in the pitch black (just as they had in the opening act of the show) to join the band. Protected prior to concert night by Holly O'Connell's **$300,000 collective student escrow ("The Forger Pot")** under Addendum No. 4 to her 1986 Cross-License—and disguised in the Marching Forgers' rehearsal folders as *"Exercise 87-B: The Anvil Finale"* with the vocal melody stripped out—for the first **1 minute and 40 seconds** (through Cassidy's spoken greeting over a lone piano chord, the Kevlar snare roll-off, and a massive 77-second AOR stadium guitar and 300-horn brass overture at `0:23–1:40`), not a single fan in the 65,000-seat stadium knew what song the band was playing, until **`1:40`** on the dot when the instruments dropped to a lone heavy kick drum and Cassidy sang the opening words of Verse 1: *"Woke up this morning, the world was gray..."*
